full_translation_en:
National Assembly
Twenty-first Session
Complete Minutes of Proceedings
20 Jestha 2083
Wednesday
Meeting Number: 94
The meeting of the National Assembly commenced today at 12:44 PM under the chairmanship of the Honourable Chairperson, Mr. Narayan Prasad Dahal.
Honourable Chairperson: Honourable members, the proceedings of today's meeting of the National Assembly commence. Honourable members, is there a new issue compared to yesterday and the day before, or is it the same issue being repeated? Therefore, Honourable members have stood up. Honourable members, please be seated. I will proceed with the business accordingly. I will provide time to some Honourable members. Honourable members, please be seated in your respective places. First, Honourable Member Sunil Bahadur Thapa, time 5 minutes.
Honourable Mr. Sunil Bahadur Thapa (Nepali Congress): Honourable Chairperson, the Prime Minister's statement a few days ago in the sovereign Parliament, the House of Representatives, that Nepal has encroached upon Indian territory is an extremely serious and unfortunate matter. This is not a matter of 'he said, she said,' because these are recorded in the audio-visuals of the House of Representatives. This is not hearsay. It is an irresponsible or immature expression. Such an expression on a matter connected to Nepal's sovereignty, national interest, and sensitive relations with a neighbouring country must be extremely responsible, clear, and based on reality. If the Prime Minister has concrete evidence to support his statement, that evidence must be presented to the Parliament and the Nepali people. If there is no such evidence, he must clearly apologize to the nation. No one has the right to create confusion on matters related to national interest. What is even more concerning is that an attempt appears to have been made to involve a third country's role or opinion on the bilateral border and geopolitical issues between Nepal and India. Matters related to Nepal's borders, sovereignty, and national interest must be resolved through dialogue between Nepal and India and established diplomatic mechanisms. Unnecessarily involving a third party in such sensitive matters is not in Nepal's interest. It can create unnecessary mistrust, confusion, and tension in Nepal-India relations. We must understand that Nepal gains nothing from any kind of Nepal-India diplomatic conflict or deadlock. Therefore, the government must adopt an extremely restrained, clear, and responsible diplomatic approach on such matters. Honourable Chairperson, the clarification issued by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs after the statement has raised further questions. The ministry stated that the Prime Minister made the remarks in the context of the complex situation regarding the border in the Susta area. Fundamentally, encroachment in the no-man's land and cross-border occupation, meaning land use rights across the border, cannot be termed as one nation encroaching on another nation's land due to technical glitches or administrative weaknesses. The chief executive of the country must be able to express his views clearly. Regardless of the clarification, damage has already been done. The Nepali people and the international community have heard the message from the Prime Minister's mouth that Nepal has encroached upon Indian territory. Unclear and contradictory statements on matters of national interest and borders have also weakened Nepal's diplomatic credibility. I would like to remind you, Honourable Chairperson, that there are examples of the then Defence Minister Mr. Sharad Singh Bhandari resigning from the Council of Ministers on 2nd Kartik 2066 (November 19, 2009) when he made a similar statement. Honourable Chairperson, sometimes wrong information or reporting from humans also leads to mistakes. For the past four days, the Prime Minister's remarks have held the Parliament hostage. The Parliament is held hostage because of the Prime Minister. Holding the Parliament hostage means holding the nation hostage. What I request is that the Prime Minister should take initiative to release this hostage. Blaming the old ones cannot be a way to escape. Therefore, I also request the Prime Minister to apologize for the inappropriate remarks made. Jai Nepal.
Honourable Chairperson: Honourable Member Bishnu Bahadur Bishwakarma, time 4 minutes.
Honourable Mr. Bishnu Bahadur Bishwakarma (Communist Party of Nepal): Honourable Chairperson, after repeated pressure from the opposition parties for the Prime Minister to attend the scheduled question-and-answer session in the House of Representatives, the Honourable Prime Minister Mr. Balendra Shah appeared in the parliamentary meeting on 17 Jestha. While responding to the questions posed by the Honourable Members of the House of Representatives, instead of answering the questions asked by the MPs, he went on to clarify baseless and fabricated matters that were not asked. He stated, 'I only found out after becoming Prime Minister that Nepalis have also encroached upon India's land,' something that Nepal, India, and even border experts were unaware of until now. By making such a fabricated, baseless, and dramatic statement that is not supported by any evidence, he not only embarrassed true Nepalis but also committed treason by speaking against the interests of Nepal. I strongly object to and condemn this secessionist statement. The Honourable Prime Minister has undermined the geographical integrity and sovereignty of the nation. Such a Prime Minister has no moral right to remain in that chair. The secessionist and traitorous Prime Minister should resign immediately. I demand his resignation. I want to ask the Honourable Prime Minister Mr. Balendra Shah, in which locations and how much land has Nepal occupied in India? I demand a response with definite facts while standing in the National Assembly. Furthermore, I demand that you appear in the National Assembly with the report on the basis of which you made the statement and provide an answer. Honourable Prime Minister, with your support, at your instigation, the Indian SSB raided the construction site of the embankment on the Narayani River in Nawalparasi district last night and created a ruckus, stopping the construction work. The construction work has been stopped through bullying, and it is because of you. This act has hurt the self-respect of 30 million Nepalis. Stopping development work with foreign troops is another act of treason and is a cowardly subservience. Do not engage in any more such acts that create discord, conflict, and destruction between Nepal and India. It would be better to resign and rest. Relations with India are currently strained. At this time of strained relations, the Prime Minister has sent the chairman of his party to India as an envoy; this is another act of sycophancy. Honourable Chairperson, as the term of the interim government is about to end and a new government is about to be formed under the leadership of Mr. Balendra Shah, India, by agreeing to open a trade route for India-China trade in Lipulek, Limpiyadhura, and Kalapani, has directly interfered in Nepal. Opening a trade route without Nepal's knowledge or consent is Indian bullying. India has occupied 6,262 hectares of land in 62 places along the border from Lipulek-Limpiyadhura to Mechi, using Nepali territory. India has been ignoring Nepal's repeated protests. This is Indian bullying of Nepal. Nepal has not occupied even an inch of Indian land so far. Now, the Honourable Prime Minister Mr. Balendra Shah's statement that Nepal has also encroached upon Indian land – is this a coincidence with India's aggression, or is it planned? We Nepalis are now concerned. It is better for you to resign and rest. Resigning is not a punishment. A moral person resigns. Your stature will be elevated by your resignation. Therefore, until your stature is elevated, this National Assembly should not proceed. Thank you.
Honourable Chairperson: Honourable Member Samjhana Devkota, time 5 minutes.
Honourable Ms. Samjhana Devkota (Communist Party of Nepal, UML): Honourable Chairperson, we are saddened that this esteemed house has been unable to function for four consecutive days. Because although the House of Representatives and the National Assembly are separate houses, we are experiencing that they are not different. After a long time since the Parliament began functioning, approximately on the 66th day of the government's formation, the Prime Minister suddenly came to Parliament and, contrary to the scheduled question-and-answer proceedings, held a press conference, and the Speaker gave him time. I consider this action and the Speaker's failure to bring this agenda item to be irresponsible steps and irresponsible work on his part as well. We easily observed his immaturity and irresponsibility. On that 17th Jestha, without study, without preparation, for the first time in the history of a head of state, it is unfortunate that he spoke against the nation's interests, nationality, self-respect, sovereignty, and the people and the country. I feel it is unfortunate. The false, misleading, irresponsible, and treasonous statement made regarding the Nepal-India border has caused the general Nepali public to express their anger from the streets to the Parliament. It is now difficult to manage. Chairperson, it is understood that the Nepal-India border relationship was determined by the Treaty of Suguali in 1816. Nepal shares more than 1850 kilometers of border with India in 27 districts. Although there is agreement in many of these places, disputes remain in many others. Primarily, Kalapani, Lipulek, and our local Susta area are still caught in disputes. There is tension there even now. Out of approximately 8,000 border pillars, about 1,240 border pillars are still missing or damaged. The Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Government of Nepal publicly stated in August 2025 that Kalapani and Lipulek are within our territory and also sent a diplomatic note. Therefore, no foreigners or any Indian entity has ever made statements about India encroaching on the border. Today, the Prime Minister of Nepal suddenly gave this response. The activities the Prime Minister has undertaken since the formation of the government are unacceptable to us. The arrest of the former Prime Minister and Home Minister at the time of government formation, the eviction of squatters and landless people without proper management, and the Prime Minister's statement on the border dispute on 17 Jestha – all these actions have raised serious questions about him. When he was the mayor, he issued a map of Greater Nepal, but how did he suddenly end up with a 'small Nepal' today? We want to tell him. The day after his statement, the chairman of Rastriya Swatantra Party went to India for a visit; we are suspicious whether there is some coordination. We are suspicious about the Speaker's ruling on such a serious matter and the silence of a party like Rastriya Swatantra Party on this serious issue. I also want to inform him. We do not have much time now. In this situation, the statement made by the Prime Minister himself is against national interest, against nationality, and is an irresponsible statement, so I feel that morally, it is not appropriate for him to continue as Prime Minister. Therefore, without misusing his position, he should resign and apologize to the general Nepali public. Thank you.

Honorable Chairperson:- Honorable members, the order of speaking during the urgent time (12:58 PM) has been placed with seriousness. Now, how many times will these matters, yesterday's and the day before's, be repeated? If we have some complex issues, some problems, one of the issues raised is alternative development finance. Now, today, it will slip away from the National Assembly. Or it will be considered that we did not do it. That bill will not come back again. Once it goes from here, it's gone. Therefore, I had thought that it would be good if we could at least move that bill forward, and that's why I took the initiative. I also had discussions with the Honorable Finance Minister of the Government of Nepal and some leaders of the parties here, as much as possible. After the discussions, I understood from the party colleagues that the matter was not resolved. Because, let me say, I had said that the Finance Minister himself should sit down and discuss it once. I was saying that there is such a difficulty in the National Assembly. And accordingly, discussions were held. During the discussions, it is one thing that there is a little bit left, something is still pending. Otherwise, for this assembly to agree to move at least one bill forward, consensus is needed to present this proposal. Because, to present it, it has become zero here. I have been saying this since yesterday. Even if we say 'maybe', it seems it won't happen. Nevertheless, thinking that the initiative should not be abandoned, the Finance Minister was called and it was done. And my special request is that you may have had some discussions with the Finance Minister, that might be one thing. My special request to the honorable members is, let's run the house, let's move forward, and at least, there are others, there are others too. As the House of Representatives has been adjourned for a week, others are not that important right now. I wish we could move forward this one bill that has come onto our shoulders. This would be another history in the history of the National Assembly, as I mentioned a history of the National Assembly yesterday. It has come to a situation where it will go back without us doing anything. It seems like we have just kept records. Therefore, my special request to the honorable members is to please sit down and cooperate in moving forward the proceedings of this bill in its proper place. And let's not create another record in the National Assembly. My special request to the honorable members is to discuss the bill that has come and move forward. Therefore, I heartily request the honorable members to take their seats and cooperate in moving forward the proceedings of the house. Honorable members, I have requested again. Please cooperate in moving forward the proceedings of the house and placing your subjects. I said this yesterday too. These subjects have been raised with seriousness before the government and among the public. I have felt this through the media as well. Therefore, since our matters have already been communicated and the government's opinion has also been sought, please cooperate in moving forward our proceedings, honorable members. Special request. Honorable members, I have requested many times, but the honorable members have not listened. Of course, why should yesterday's words be used? However, the National Assembly, according to the recognition of all, according to the recognition of the entire country, is an institution that guides the government, even the House of Representatives, with suggestions. This is a common understanding among the public. The National Assembly is known as an institution that corrects the deteriorating situation of the country and moves forward, giving suggestions to everyone. Therefore, the recent developments and circumstances in the country, and the situation that has arisen between the Honorable Prime Minister and the opposition parties represented in the House of Representatives, have made the entire country agitated again, let us understand this. Therefore, I feel that it is our responsibility to manage that agitated situation, and we have been managing it until today. That is why I believe that we should conduct the house to manage that situation and move forward, and we should be able to give suggestions not only to the government but also to the House of Representatives with seriousness. This is the recognition of the National Assembly, please do not forget this, and please cooperate in moving forward these proceedings accordingly. My special request. Honorable members, the next meeting of the National Assembly will be held on Saturday, Jestha 26, 2083, at 1:15 PM, and this meeting is adjourned. (Thereafter, the next meeting was adjourned to be held on Saturday, Jestha 26, 2083, at 1:15 PM.) Adjourned: 13:07 PM.

sections.summary_en: The National Assembly meeting commenced under the chairmanship of Narayan Prasad Dahal. The chairperson noted that the agenda might be a repeat of previous discussions and asked members to be seated before proceeding.

speakers.name: Narayan Prasad Dahal
speakers.topic: Opening the session and managing member participation

sections.name: Main Business
sections.summary_en: Honourable Member Sunil Bahadur Thapa raised concerns about the Prime Minister's statement regarding Nepal encroaching on Indian territory, demanding clarification and an apology if evidence is lacking. He emphasized resolving border issues through bilateral dialogue and warned against involving third parties. Honourable Member Bishnu Bahadur Bishwakarma strongly condemned the Prime Minister's statement as treasonous and demanded his resignation, questioning the basis of the claim and highlighting alleged Indian interference in development projects. Honourable Member Samjhana Devkota also criticized the Prime Minister's statement as irresponsible and against national interest, demanding his resignation and an apology.

sections.summary_en: The speaker expresses frustration that important bills, like the alternative development finance bill, are not being advanced due to lack of consensus. Despite previous discussions with the Finance Minister and party leaders, progress has stalled. The speaker urges members to cooperate to move the bill forward and avoid setting a negative precedent for the National Assembly.
